summary: DECISION-030 cannot be implemented literally for the pinned XNAS MBO bytes because one normalized Nasdaq execution can contain same-sequence T, F, and C records that each carry LAST. Immediate LAST closure would split one execution into three completed groups, count two execution groups, and publish pre-cancel book state. A terminal-sequence-block repair changes both the accepted closure rule and causal availability rule, so it requires separate operator authority.

implementation_boundary.reason_no_code_change: The contradiction is in the accepted event-boundary specification, not a remediable implementation defect. Encoding a terminal-sequence lookahead without new authority would silently change the estimand and its causal timing.

reference_decoder.source_ordinal_definition: One-based body-record position in reference CLI NDJSON output.

measurement_definition.population: Every decoded body record in both pinned 2025-07-03 files.

reducer.ordering: Reference decoder source order; no sort, join, deduplication, or timestamp reordering.
reducer.flush_rule: Flush the current sequence block when the projected block key changes and once at clean EOF.
reducer.record_count: Increment once for every projected body record.
reducer.sequence_blocks: Increment once for every flushed nonempty maximal contiguous block.
reducer.repeated_last_sequence_blocks: Increment when sum((flags div 128) mod 2) > 1 inside the block.
reducer.tfc_sequence_blocks: Increment when the MBO block contains at least one T, at least one F, and at least one C.
reducer.tfc_all_last_sequence_blocks: Increment when the MBO block is T/F/C-bearing and last_count == block_record_count.
reducer.tfc_no_last_sequence_blocks: Increment when the MBO block is T/F/C-bearing and last_count == 0.
reducer.execution_bearing_terminal_sequence_bloc: Increment when the MBO block contains T or F and last_count > 0.
reducer.tc_sequence_blocks: Increment when the MBP-10 block contains at least one T and at least one C.
reducer.tc_all_last_sequence_blocks: Increment when the MBP-10 block is T/C-bearing and last_count == block_record_count.

measurement_definition.sequence_block_definition: A maximal contiguous source-order run with the stated key.
measurement_definition.tfc_all_last_definition: A sequence block contains T, F, and C and every member has LAST set.
measurement_definition.tfc_no_last_definition: A sequence block contains T, F, and C and no member has LAST set.
measurement_definition.tc_all_last_definition: An MBP-10 sequence block contains T and C and every member has LAST set.

cross_schema_checks.interpretation: The repeated-LAST pattern is systematic and corroborated in the separately encoded provider-derived MBP-10 companion. The two schemas share upstream venue/provider lineage and are not statistically independent. The agreement rules out an isolated malformed MBO record.

flag_semantics.pinned_dbn_v0_20_0_interpretation: The pinned source names bit 0x80 as LAST but does not name bit 0x02.
flag_semantics.current_databento_documentation_interpre: Current Databento documentation names bit 0x02 F_PUBLISHER_SPECIFIC and states that its meaning depends on the publisher.
flag_semantics.qualification: The XNAS meaning of bit 0x02 is unresolved under the pinned decoder contract. The blocker uses only the raw byte and the pinned LAST mask; it does not infer closure semantics from the publisher-specific bit.
flag_semantics.impact: The unresolved publisher-specific bit strengthens the fail-closed disposition and forbids generalizing the observed pattern to another publisher.

multi_sequence_terminal_event_mbo.interpretation_limit: This window proves that sequence cannot be a universal completed-event key. It does not by itself authorize a new grouping rule.

rejected_silent_repairs.repair: Treat every LAST-bearing record as an independent completed event.
rejected_silent_repairs.reason: Splits one normalized Nasdaq execution, double-counts executions, and exposes the pre-C book.

rejected_silent_repairs.repair: Group every record with the same venue sequence.
rejected_silent_repairs.reason: Fails the observed multi-sequence event and contradicts DECISION-030's instruction that sequence is validation evidence rather than the sole group identity.

rejected_silent_repairs.repair: Treat repeated LAST inside a terminal sequence block as one terminator and close on the next different-sequence record.
rejected_silent_repairs.reason: Scientifically plausible for pinned XNAS bytes, but it changes the accepted closure rule and requires a later closure witness.

rejected_silent_repairs.repair: Use max member ts_recv after terminal-sequence lookahead.
rejected_silent_repairs.reason: Backdates knowledge of closure. If the later boundary witness is required, causal availability must include the witness observation time.
EOF provides no timestamped causal market-data witness and cannot safely be backdated.

remediation_accounting.reason: Every candidate that joins repeated-LAST records changes the accepted event-boundary rule. Every causal implementation that waits for a boundary witness also changes the accepted availability rule. Neither change is an implementation-only remediation authorized by the accepted bytes.
remediation_accounting.decision_030_second_failure_clause: Section 6 allows one remediation and requires the named blocker after a second conformance failure; it does not require an unavailable or specification-changing remediation.
remediation_accounting.controlling_terminal_authority: Section 2 ends the bounded authorization when a terminal blocker is emitted, the required-artifact order allows each cycle to end with one explicit blocker, and the acceptance record states that the first gate either passes or records one terminal blocker.
remediation_accounting.why_terminal_now: No conforming completed-event implementation can be written under current authority. Continuing would either knowingly emit false groups or silently supersede accepted governance.

minimum_superseding_clarification.scope: Pinned XNAS.ITCH normalization only; no cross-publisher generalization.
required_points: Define a same-identity terminal sequence block and the handling of repeated LAST inside it.
